label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §1.1…: Quasi-realism: moral sentences can be true or false…
locator: §1.1, 'Others deny that their contents are true or false in any robust sense but not that they can be true or false in a deflationary sense'
interpretation: Most current non-cognitivists accept the negative theses only in a weakened form; some deny robust truth or falsity of moral contents but allow deflationary truth and falsity, 'according to which there is no substantial property separating true and false sentences'. Read as the quasi-realist's minimal truth: moral sentences are minimally, not robustly, truth-apt (Blackburn, Gibbard: §2.3). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
